relations.subject: tool:cbanalyze-core
relations.evidence: The `cbanalyze-core` tool cannot analyze minidump core files and should only be used when directed by Couchbase Support.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike cbcollect-info-tool.md, this page never states that root/administrator privileges are needed, even though it is functionally the same kind of Couchbase-Support-directed diagnostic tool operating on the same class of low-level system artifact (a core dump vs. a log bundle). No RBAC or OS-privilege statement of any kind appears. Also absent: any description of the report file's format or contents - the -f flag is documented only as 'Use the specified file for output', with no schema, unlike cbcollect_info's detailed Table 2.

cross_component_finding: This is one of three standalone, non-subcommand-structured diagnostic tools in this batch (with cbcollect-info-tool.md and finderr.md) - each a single-purpose executable with a two-line syntax and no command tree, in contrast to the cbstats/cbepctl/cbft-bleve families which each anchor a multi-page subcommand structure. This supports the round's framing that couchbase-server, cbcollect-info, cbanalyze-core and finderr sit outside the CLI-subcommand pattern entirely.
